Ethan — thanks for the details you shared on the call. Quick technical sketch and conservative savings estimates based on your numbers:

1) Batching strategy (per-route):
   - Use dynamic batching window tuned to 50–100ms for low-latency flows; target batch sizes 8–16 tokens for short requests and up to 64 for report jobs.
   - Expected p95 impact: +20–40ms; stays within your 300–500ms SLO for the majority of traffic.

2) Caching & KV prefix reuse:
   - We recommend prefix/KV caching for frequent template prompts (you mentioned ~15% of traffic is templated). That can reduce token generation by ~12–18% on those routes.

3) Quantization profile recommendations:
   - Mixed 4-bit for non-sensitive routes (int4 + tuned kernels): ~1.7–2.2x speedup, 30–50% GPU memory reduction.
   - int8 (symmetric) for highest-throughput routes where determinism is less critical: ~2.5x throughput improvement vs fp16 in our internal tests.

4) Combined unit-economics (conservative):
   - Baseline hosted per-token cost (no Optimize): assume $0.000X per token (we'll plug real numbers in the proposal).
   - With batching + caching + 4-bit quantization: expected token-cost reduction of ~35–55% depending on route mix.

I attached a short spreadsheet with scenario math: quant-scenarios.xlsx (estimations only). For the pilot we can enable monitoring hooks (per-route cost dashboards) so you see delta live.

If you want, we can run a 2-week controlled pilot on a small subset of traffic to validate p95 and unit cost before broader rollout.

—Ben
